R3-RTV5-01.repair: New versioned binding artifacts/evaluation-proof.v1.json rather than an overload of retention. Proof obligations are declared per claim shape. Relationship matches require an ordered edge witness with endpoints, relationKind and a resolvable factRef plus a relationSemanticsRef — subject/span metadata cannot satisfy them. Verdict derivation recomputes the complete outcome-set commitment over every activated evaluation. no-match and aggregate sets are recomputed from the retained fact partition, not asserted. One canonical commitment grammar replaces the two conflicting ones: domain-tagged, length-prefixed, deduplicated, sorted, full 64-hex, truncation FORBIDDEN.

R3-RTV5-02.repair: retention-tiers.v6 capabilityClosure binds a host-owned capability-requirement closure mapping every reference in the proof graph to exactly one retention unit at the MINIMUM capability that needs it, with a recomputable closure commitment. RC-12 adds the rule v5 lacked entirely: a unit is available only if EVERY object it contains is available, so partial availability retains no authority.
R3-RTV5-02.closesCounterexample: R3-RTV5-CE-03 — CL-NEG-01 (omitted predicate-semantics unit) and CL-NEG-03 (predicate unit downgraded to replayable while a verifiable no-match depends on it) both reject via RC-11.
R3-RTV5-02.checkerCoverage: 8 closure fixtures: 3 accepting (including replay-closure loss demoting replayable→verifiable), 5 rejecting (omission, alias, downgrade, non-recomputing commitment, partial availability).
R3-RTV5-02.residualEvidence: The closure is derived from a proof graph the same author designed. Cost of recomputing it for a Run with many thousands of units is unmeasured.

R3-RTV5-03.repair: Boolean resolvedAtAdmission is replaced by resolve-and-pin: ONE ledger transaction that resolves effective capability and acquires a durable read lease. Read leases and purge leases share one lock domain ordered by ledger sequence, so a purge cannot miss a reader. Six transitions LP-1..LP-6 cover purge-vs-held-lease (rejected, retryable), purge-before-admission, PURGE-PREPARED tombstone, crash reclamation, expiry-during-use, and idempotent retry.
R3-RTV5-03.closesCounterexample: R3-RTV5-CE-04 — LP-5 states expiry does not preempt a live lease and LP-1 states purge is rejected rather than racing, which is the actual TOCTOU closure.
R3-RTV5-03.checkerCoverage: 6 lease fixtures, each bound to a transition and to a D9 row that must DERIVE. Mutations prove the atomicity declaration, the durable lease record, and the contention outcome are all load-bearing.
R3-RTV5-03.residualEvidence: Specification only. No crash-injection harness and no real ledger. v6 explicitly states it does not claim runtime atomicity from a document.

R3-RTV5-04.decision: ACCEPTED — v5's promise is WITHDRAWN, not defended
R3-RTV5-04.repair: v5 promised targeted purge removes the selected material AND leaves unrelated Runs untouched AND never rewrites sealed identity. Reviewer-3 proved those three cannot all hold for a shared partition. The purge key is now the content-addressed OBJECT within one ProjectId namespace. Objects containing the selection are partitioned into UNBLOCKED (removed) and BLOCKED (retained and reported with blocking Run IDs), matching threat-model deletionProtocol.sharedObjectRule. Removing blocked material requires explicitly purging the blocking Runs — a separate stronger operation, consistent with architecture/06 'reports blocked pins and requires an explicit stronger operation to break them'.
R3-RTV5-04.closesCounterexample: R3-RTV5-CE-05 — PF-02 asserts the shared partition is reported blocked, never removed; PF-03 asserts no out-of-scope Run is demoted.
R3-RTV5-04.honestNarrowing: Subject-level isolation inside a shared partition is NOT provided. This is carried as residual RC-R-01 and must reach the product contract: a user asking to purge a subject may be told the subject survives in shared retained material.
R3-RTV5-04.checkerCoverage: 4 purge fixtures; the removed/blocked partition is RECOMPUTED from reachability rather than trusted. Mutations reject removing a blocked object and demoting an out-of-scope Run.
R3-RTV5-04.residualEvidence: Joined against storage-namespace.adjudication-admission-storage-lane.v1 at a point in time. If that lane changes reference-count or purge semantics these rules must be re-derived.

R3-RTV5-05.repair: RC-10 no longer checks vocabulary membership. check-retention-custody.py imports check-d9.py — which d9-exit-contract.v1.6 names as referenceDerivation.implementation — and asserts each row's declared class and code are what derive_class/derive_codes DERIVE from complete axes. Ten rows now distinguish terminal authorized loss (REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE) from transient outage (HOST.IO_FAILURE), ledger corruption (LEDGER.CORRUPT), object materialisation failure (CAS.LINK_FAILED), missing identity with and without a tombstone (IDENTITY.EXPIRED / IDENTITY.UNKNOWN), lease contention (LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT) and the previously omitted admitted completeness query (QUERY.COMPLETENESS_UNMET → indeterminate).
R3-RTV5-05.closesProbe: R3-PROBE-04 — a wrong class carrying an in-vocabulary code is now rejected by derivation.
R3-RTV5-05.closesCounterexample: R3-RTV5-CE-06 — transient OUTAGE no longer shares a code with terminal purge; a dedicated check rejects that collapse.
R3-RTV5-05.d9NotReopened: No new reason or error code. Every required distinction already existed in D9's closed maps, so d9-exit-contract.v1.6 is untouched and its 44 goldens are undisturbed.
R3-RTV5-05.checkerCoverage: requiredDistinctions makes coverage itself checkable — dropping a row now fails rather than silently removing a remedy class.
R3-RTV5-05.residualEvidence: The rows enumerate situations this contract knows about. Totality over all future operations is not proved.
